options.a: One global type; categories subscribe (join table)
options.b: Each category owns its own copy
options.a′: One global type, subscribed, with a per-membership display name (Shopify's extended attributes)
options.d: No category-scoped attribute concept at all
options.AMB: Ambiguous, by the record's own admission

subtallies.name: Counting every row (14 — Tokopedia's eras separate)
Holding every hedged row out (the honest margin)

framing: On most platforms the attribute-owning object is NOT the browse category — Magento's eav_attribute_set, Akeneo's Family, commercetools'/Amazon's/Walmart's ProductType, Salesforce's object type + category groups. Only Shopify, eBay, Shopee, Tokopedia merge the two, and Lock 1 merges them for us. The (c) column is empty: no platform ships a shared definition with a per-category value list (commercetools is (c) on values, (b) on the object). Counter-finding: Shopify does not reuse one Flavor across domains — it mints more global types (Flavor 293 categories/30 values · Pet food flavor 43/54 · Baby food flavor 41/4 · E-liquid flavor 22/10; 329 size-like definitions, 219 on ≤1 category). (a)'s headline benefit — one filter across categories — materialises for Color (11,730 edges), Pattern (11,686), Material (4,546), not for flavour or size.

rows.h: name-PK registry + ProductTypeAttribute join; legacy XSD surface behaves like (b)
rows.shape: “name is stable; the label is not. Every one of the 381 legacy …/Flavor XPaths maps to exactly one JSON pointer — /attributes/flavor/0/value”; “Requiredness is a property of this join, not of the Attribute. The same attribute is required for one product type and optional for another.” Measured: 213 product types → 208 distinct attributes, 1,154 pairs. Hedge: on the legacy XSD surface divergence is real — 101–124 names with differing maxLength measured (149–157 on the complete set). Inference for why: a JSON Schema is compiled per (type × marketplace × parentage level) with monthly deltas; a stable name lets a schema be regenerated without invalidating stored values; the join is mutable (15,299 of 26,135 flavour release-note rows are “attribute deleted and no longer associated with the product type”).

rows.h: on two surfaces: taxonomy join + metafield constraint list
rows.shape: Taxonomy: 8,240 base attributes, 93,007 category→attribute edges; “Extended attributes are aliases — no values of their own … they reuse the base attribute's GID” — 316 extended names over 2,891 edges, the mechanism behind option (a′). Metafields: “Currently, Shopify only supports constraint subtypes that correspond to product categories on Product metafield definitions.” — one definition, a constraint list of category ids (7,750 on shopify.color-pattern). Stated rationale for the constraint: “Shoe size is a valid metafield for Shoes but wouldn't apply to Sweaters.” No statement explains why the taxonomy attribute is global rather than per node. Live 2026-09-21 (Admin API 2026-07): Flavor is one gid (TaxonomyAttribute/1458) with the identical 30 {id, name} values on Chocolate, Snack Foods, Snack Cakes, Soda, Coffee and Coffee Cakes; absent on Pasta & Noodles and Condiments — one global type, per-category membership, no per-category value list.

rows.h: the record withdrew half its own claim — three attributes are availability-gated by category
rows.shape: “There is no per-category attribute schema. The bag is one global set: 145 properties in Merchant API products_v1.” Instrument: categoryAttribute|category_attribute|attributesFor|productTypeDefinition|schemaFor → 0. Inference: Google receives a flat feed from sellers it does not control; a per-category schema would require every seller to resolve a taxonomy node before serialising a row.

rows.h: the strongest (b): no object identity exists
rows.shape: “Each category has a different set of aspects and different requirements for aspect values.” “There is no identifier on an aspect or an aspect value.” — aspectId 0 · valueId 0 · aspectValueId 0 · "id": 0. Two leaves carrying Flavor cannot be one object. Inference: aspect lists are versioned per (category_tree_id, category_id, marketplace); per-leaf materialisation lets a set change without a global migration — the same category id under two trees returns two different aspect lists.

rows.h: the only platform that measures how far the copies diverge
rows.shape: “Every attribute is written out in full at every product type; nothing is referenced.” 6,576 names written out 383,947 times; 1,767 have more than one distinct definition — flavor 50, color 126, size 438. Vendor states the consequence, not the reason: “Based on the chosen Product Type, attribute requirements, values, and recommendations will vary.”

rows.h: declared ambiguous by the record itself (open item U-8)
rows.shape: “Each product category has different attribute data.” and v2.product.search_attribute_value_list is keyed by attribute_id alone, with no category_id — value rows belong to the attribute. Open: “Whether an attribute_id is shared across categories or re-minted per category.” Shopee publishes no attribute inventory, no value inventory, no category file — nothing to count.

rows.h: Era A ambiguous leaning (a); Era B (a) on one route
rows.shape: Era A: “Variant / VariantUnit / VariantUnitValue — the global axis catalogue”, retrieved for a category_id; the record calls it global and the ids look global, but no second category's response was ever retrieved; the parallel Annotation system has no stable id and is (b)-shaped. Era B: attributes “bound to the specified category”, yet the changelog's “Imported Goods” attribute is one id (102254) with one value pair (1000058/1000059) “to all categories except digital” — one id across every category but one. Single route (a changelog), so nothing moved to VERIFIED.

“After a custom attribute definition is set to be applicable to an object … that definition is available for all objects of that type.” — a “flavour” definition allowed on ITEM appears on every item in the seller's catalogue. Inference: single-tenant seller tooling where the merchant authors both categories and attributes; the 10+10 cap removes the problem scoping would solve.

rows.h: the only one with genuine inheritance down the category tree
rows.shape: “An attribute group is a grouping of attribute assignments that's attached to a category. Attributes can belong to more than one attribute group.” The attribute model = the global product attribute groups + the classification category's groups + “product attribute groups of any parent categories”. Override order (“the sub-category group overrides the parent group”) is single-route. Rationale only “to help you manage product attributes”; inference: a single-tenant storefront where the merchant owns the tree, so inheritance costs nothing.

rows.h: the subscriber is the Family, not the category
rows.shape: “Family owns the attribute set, through a many-to-many join table — an attribute is reusable across families.” Vendor: “A product family can use all of the attributes available in the PIM. Several families of products can use the same attributes.” Clearest stated purpose of any: “The family helps managing the product's completeness as you can say at the family level, which family attributes are required for the completeness calculation.”

rows.h: global definition registry; the one unhedged “no” in #11031's tally
rows.shape: woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies: six columns, “none of them references a category, a product type, or any grouping object”; 500 product_cat lines, 0 also match attribute_taxonom. The only explicit design rationale for globality in the thirteen: “Attributes can be defined globally, so they’re easy to update across the entire store, and available to be used on any product, or … defined individually, at the product level, and they will only exist for that single product.”

rows.h: (b) on the object, (c) on the values; name-uniqueness scope is an open contradiction (U6)
rows.shape: AttributeDefinition is “Not a resource: no id, no version; reached only through its ProductType”; “the enum values can be different for each ProductType” / “To use the same name in multiple ProductTypes, each AttributeDefinition must have the same type.” The only explicit argument for per-type scoping: a T-Shirt type has Color = Red/Green/Blue, a Jeans type has Color = Blue/Black/Grey; “You wouldn't ask for the Neckline of a pair of jeans, would you? By defining appropriate Attribute types for each Product Type, you prevent irrelevant or nonsensical data from being entered.” Contradiction: resource doc says name “unique within the Project”, draft doc says “unique within the ProductType”.

rows.h: one flavor row per entity type; membership via eav_entity_attribute
rows.shape: eav_attribute UNIQUE (entity_type_id, attribute_code); “the attribute-owning object exists and it is the attribute set … a product points at exactly one, through a single NOT NULL scalar column” (attribute_set_id); membership = eav_entity_attribute rows. Merged-list proof: customAttributeMetadata lists 20 size options — the union of the two fixture lists. Adobe states the purpose of the set: “The attribute set determines the fields that are available during data entry, and the values that appear to the customer.” The browse category plays no part in any schema table.
